layers.note: A prostrate evergreen shrub of open, dry ground: gravel, rock and open pine woods.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −30 to 8 °C; gone below −40 °C and above 12 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −48 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −55 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 24 °C; gone below 4 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 600 to 6,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 300.

degree_days_5.note: About 150 to 3,800 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 50.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.25, gone by 0.15.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Kinnikinnick grows around the northern hemisphere, in North America from Alaska to New Mexico and across Canada (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
